bull_bear.body:
- Subsidiary of Coal India Limited (CIL holds a 90% stake), giving parentage and support from the Ministry of Coal
- Miniratna PSU status with an established position as one of the leading producers of coking coal in India — it produces bulk of the coking coal mined in the country
- Resource base concentrated in the Jharia and Raniganj coalfields, which contain important coking coal resources
- Coal beneficiation infrastructure — a washery network being expanded and modernized, including new washeries commissioned with a combined capacity of 7.00 million tonnes per year
- Policy tailwind: coking coal notified as a 'Critical and Strategic Mineral' by the Government of India, reinforcing national focus on indigenous production and import substitution
- Diversified consumer base across power, steel, fertilizer and other industrial sectors
- Experienced workforce, ongoing modernization initiatives and strategic growth projects
- Well-established internal control system, with accounts subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Reserve concentration and eventual exhaustion in Jharia and Raniganj — Mines and washeries are concentrated in Jharia, Jharkhand and Raniganj, West Bengal; eventual exhaustion of coal reserves in these areas, or an inability to successfully exploit existing reserves, may adversely affect the business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- Critical surface infrastructure over the leasehold constrains mining — Coal-bearing areas under the Company's leasehold are traversed by major railway lines (D.C Railway line, Main JC Railway line and Adra - Gomoh Railway line), roads and other public utilities; mining in such areas needs extensive planning, regulatory approvals and protective measures, affecting operational flexibility and project implementation timelines.
- Geological, technical and operational hazards including mine fires and subsidence — Operations are subject to mine fires, subsidence, water inundation, complex geological conditions, old underground workings and reserve estimation uncertainties, which may affect production, productivity, project implementation and operating costs. Illegal mining exposing coal to air, aggravating spontaneous combustion, is separately flagged as a threat.
- Land acquisition, rehabilitation and resettlement delays and land-record disputes — Delays in land acquisition, R&R of affected families, disputes over land records and difficulty in obtaining physical possession of acquired land may affect project execution and expansion plans; discrepancies between Cadastral Survey (CS) and Revisional Settlement (RS) Khatiyan records compound this, causing legal complications and delays. Inability to establish physical possession of land acquired under the LA Act is listed among threats.
- Legacy mine fires, dense habitation and implementation of the Revised Jharia Master Plan — The Company operates in a region affected by legacy mine fires and subsidence; effective implementation of R&R measures under the Revised Jharia Master Plan is important for safeguarding inhabitants in vulnerable areas, and challenges may give rise to safety, social and operational concerns. Dense habitation over coal-bearing areas hinders statutory permissions for depillaring and blasting, and delays in relocating occupants and unauthorized encroachers may affect extraction plans. Delay in the Jharia Master Plan is flagged as endangering lives of habitants and risking loss of coal reserve in fire beneath.
- Supply chain, contractor dependence and input cost escalation — Operations depend on timely availability of explosives, diesel, spare parts, equipment, transportation infrastructure and contractor services; disruption in supply chain, logistics or contractor performance may adversely affect mining and production, while escalation in the cost of contractual services, fuel, explosives, transportation and equipment maintenance may impact operating costs and profitability.
- Revenue concentration in coking coal and steel-sector demand / technology shift — A significant portion of the Company's revenue is derived from coking coal; changes in demand from the steel sector, technological changes in steelmaking, increased use of alternative materials or fuels, or adverse market conditions may affect demand for the Company's products. Scarcity of consumers for the sale of reject generated at washeries is a further flagged threat.
- Environmental regulation and extreme weather / physical climate exposure — Operations are exposed to environmental risks, evolving regulatory requirements and extreme weather events including heavy rainfall, which may impact production, overburden removal, coal evacuation and overall operational performance; the Company notes specific energy consumption rose during the year due to enhanced dewatering requirement from a heavy monsoon.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: BCCL is engaged in mining of coal and allied activities, largely in Jharkhand and marginally in West Bengal, with operations concentrated in the Jharia Coalfield of Jharkhand and the Raniganj Coalfield of West Bengal. It operates in a single business segment, viz., coal mining and allied activities, producing raw coking and non-coking coal and beneficiating coking and power coal through its washeries. The Company caters to a diversified consumer base comprising power utilities, steel producers, fertilizer units and other industrial consumers, and plays a strategic role in supporting the domestic steel industry through production and beneficiation of coking coal.

outlook.body:
- Enhance operational efficiency, improve coal quality, augment production capacity and maximize value from the resource base through modern technologies and innovative operating models
- Strengthen coal beneficiation infrastructure and expand washing capacity to improve availability and quality of washed coking coal and reduce import dependence
- Operationalize and monetize identified discontinued mines and washeries through MDO/WDO models to unlock value from existing infrastructure
- Continue departmental production alongside Hiring of HEMMs in suitable projects
- Technological intervention through deployment of high-capacity mining equipment and modern mining methods to improve productivity, enhance recovery and access otherwise inaccessible reserves
- Reorganisation of mining operations under long-term mine planning to enable scientific and large-scale extraction of deep seated coal resources
- Continuous identification and development of new producing patches and optimization of mining infrastructure
- Sustainable mining and energy transition through expansion of renewable energy capacity and environmentally responsible mining practices
- Develop Coal Bed Methane (CBM) resources within leasehold areas as a diversification and long-term value creation lever
- Marketing focus on customer engagement, supply reliability and strengthening presence in key consumer sectors through consistent supply of quality coal products
- BCCL is a Miniratna PSU and a subsidiary of Coal India Limited, and its capital-allocation framework is governed by Board-approved policies rather than a stated numeric payout target. The Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy, which along with its CSR Policy, Whistle Blower Policy, Related Party Policy, Materiality Policy and Preservation of Documents and Archival Policy is uploaded on the Company's website; the Practising Company Secretary has affirmed that all applicable policies under SEBI Regulations are adopted with the approval of the board of directors and are reviewed and timely updated. Reinvestment intent is directed at capacity augmentation and modernization of mining operations, expansion of beneficiation (washery) capacity and renewable energy capacity, while capital is recycled through asset monetisation — operationalising discontinued mines under the MDO mode, monetising old washeries under the WDO route, and engaging a transaction advisor for monetisation of the Moonidih Captive Power Plant. The Company confirms it has no subsidiary or material subsidiary, and there are no loans to related parties (Directors, Key Managerial Persons and others), nor any trade or other receivables due from directors or officers.
- Committed to sustainable mining and energy transition initiatives through expansion of renewable energy capacity, efficient resource utilisation and adoption of environmentally responsible mining practices
- Installation of solar power plants identified as a stated opportunity within the Company's command area, reducing dependency on conventional sources of energy
- Development of Coal Bed Methane (CBM) resources within leasehold areas — recovery and utilization of CBM provides an alternative source of energy, improves resource utilization and supports sustainable mining practices
- Energy conservation programme in FY 2025-26: replacement of conventional lights with LED lighting in mines, offices and residential colonies with 9898 LED lights installed; 120 energy-efficient ACs; 08 e-vehicles; 33 energy-efficient motors; 89 units of 16M high mast lighting towers with 8X400W LED fittings; and 89 auto timer switches
- Circular use of mining waste: the 2x10 MW Moonidih captive power plant was installed for utilization of washery rejects
- Social licence and community safety: implementation of rehabilitation and resettlement measures under the Revised Jharia Master Plan to safeguard inhabitants residing in fire-affected and subsidence-prone zones
- Coal beneficiation as an environmental and import-substitution lever — improving washed coking coal availability for the domestic steel sector
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: BCCL's expansion during FY 2025-26 centred on reviving discontinued assets and building out beneficiation and renewable capacity. Production commenced from the PB Project, the first discontinued mine operationalised under the Company's asset monetisation initiative through the Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) mode, and the Company completed construction of the 2.0 MTPA Bhojudih Coal Washery, which is expected to strengthen coal beneficiation infrastructure and improve availability of quality coking coal. Looking forward, the Company is pursuing operationalization and monetization of identified discontinued mines and washeries through MDO/WDO models, expansion of washing capacity to support the requirement of quality coking coal and reduce import dependence, deployment of high-capacity mining equipment and modern mining methods, and reorganisation of mining operations to enable scientific and large-scale extraction of deep seated coal resources. On the power and renewable side, a 25 MW ground-mounted solar power plant at Bhojudih Coal Washery in Purulia District is ongoing, with comprehensive O&M of the plant and associated transmission system for 5 years thereafter; upcoming projects comprise a 25 MW ground-mounted solar plant at Moonidih and a 25 MW ground-mounted solar plant at Dugdha Washery (Phase-II), each including O&M for a period of 10 years. These add to 7.97 MW of rooftop and 20 MW of ground-mounted solar already installed and commissioned up to FY 2025-26. Separately, BCCL has appointed SBICAP as Transaction Advisor cum Consultant for asset monetization of the 2x10 MW Moonidih Captive Power Plant, and the advisor's report is under examination. Energy-conservation capex during the year included installation of 9898 LED lights, 120 energy-efficient ACs, 08 e-vehicles, 33 energy-efficient motors, 89 units of 16M high mast lighting towers, 89 auto timer switches and 94 energy-efficient super fans, with a purchase order to be placed for a 4000 KVAR capacitor bank.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for coal is expected to remain supported by growth in power generation, infrastructure development and industrial activity in the country
- Coal demand is driven by growth in power generation, industrial production, infrastructure development and overall economic activity; the power sector remained the largest consumer of the Company's coal supplies during FY 2025-26
- India continues to depend substantially on imported coking coal — imports increased to 66.33 million tonnes from 57.58 million tonnes in the previous year — underscoring the domestic demand-supply gap and the opportunity for indigenous production
- Notification of coking coal as a 'Critical and Strategic Mineral' under the MMDR Act, 1957 reinforces the national focus on increasing indigenous production and beneficiation, an import-substitution tailwind under Atmanirbhar Bharat
- Expansion of washing capacity is expected to improve product quality, strengthen customer satisfaction, enhance value realization and support import substitution efforts
- Product mix lever: shifting toward beneficiated / washed coking coal for the steel sector to enhance value realization
- Operating headwinds flagged: geological complexities, legacy mine fires, land acquisition, rehabilitation and resettlement requirements, environmental compliance, evacuation infrastructure constraints and weather-related disruptions
- Cost pressure risk from escalation in contractual services, fuel, explosives, transportation and equipment maintenance
